title_en: The Chapter of the Religious Garb
translit:
|| ath shri Bhekhka ang ||13||

mala tilak Jivana | e Vishnuka bhekh ||
sharire shobha dekhiye | pan Hari vina pura pret ||1||
dou barabar Jivana | swangi aur sansar ||
bhekh banayo bhagatko | mito na unko aahar ||2||
sabar mathe singdan | aiso mala bhekh ||
jhujh kaiso tahan Jivana | jahan rajbansi nahi rekh ||3||
mala bharunse Jivana | gayo janmaro banjh ||
Sitapati Raghunathki | swapne nahi avaj ||4||
hath katun ta daaska | jo mala bandhe mand ||
Ram naam bin Jivana | bhekh kiyo sab bhand ||5||
mala paheri be char | manman harakhe murkha ||
e gatrandani naar | phokat deve pharadka ||6||
lambo japmalo Jivana | duniyakun dekhlay ||
adha naamsun kaam hai | je Sadguru diya batay ||7||
tilak tulsi bharunse tare | te jug to koi aur ||
ab Kaljug kahe sun Jivana | mere naam bina nahi thaur ||8||
pani pahele Jivana | tun mojan mat utar ||
Ram naam rude nahi | to kyon chhute sansar ||9||
paras bin parse nahi | jyun lohakun pashan ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | phokat bhekh aur gnan ||10||
bhagal vidya sab bhekhman | aap kahave daas ||
Brahmadik khele Jivana | ante gaye niras ||11||
tak trevad Trikam bin | kaiso jog vairag ||
o naar dohagan Jivana | je Shame diyo sohag ||12||
banjh piyare putrakun | hasi hasi mangal gay ||
maat putraki Jivana | mukh mudi muskay ||13||
kaun karmase Jivana | banjh bhai je naar ||
Jashodae jayo davdo | mangal na gaye dwar ||14||
bhekh banayo bhagatko | nahi naam pratit ||
banjh mangal jyun Jivana | aan putra par prit ||15||
sakh shabd ko kare | nahi na Raghupati naam ||
hunsh ghevarki Jivana | ane gaanth na kodi daam ||16||
thagal thigal sab koi kare | do do akshar jod ||
gudli vanaje Jivana | kyun paiye lakh kod ||17||
it utathe Jivana | shikh lai do char ||
aage jai pandit bhayo | so kabahu na pave paar ||18||
man guru charane arpiye | tan he kul pach manhi ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | yun Harijan kahavat nahi ||19||
aiso ajar hai Jivana | jaat paat kul jay ||
aur baatanki baat hai | Brahmadik chale thagay ||20||
hani puni Jivana | sab koi dhare vairag ||
jaise ke taise bhaye | mukh muchh shir pagh ||21||
Kaustubh mani kote dhare | bich bich kukar haad ||
Ram bhaktiman Jivana | Anadev sanskar ||22||
vairagi vivek bin | mange ghar ghar bhikh ||
sarvas Hari de Jivana | jo mane guruki shikh ||23||
juthan chate jagatki | manman dhare abhiman ||
e gurukripa nahi Jivana | jem ghar ghar bhatke shwan ||24||
man mundchyo nahi Jivana | to shir munde kaha hoy ||
gatrandasa dekhiye | nahi purush nahi joy ||25||
mund mundaye kaha bhayo | kaha badhave kesh ||
aapo na mite Jivana | van Sadguru updesh ||26||
tilak dhare de bandagi | lal chhadi le hath ||
e Jam govalo sun Jivana | le chalo sab sath ||27||
jyun nimala puchhka | tyun nimala muchh ||
Ramnaam bin Jivana | aisi modhe muchh ||28||
Ram naam sab ko kahe | apne apne unman ||
aapo na mite Jivana | kyon chhute chare khan ||29||
Gorakh sab jogi kahe | sanyasi kahe Datt ||
aatam dharam bin Jivana | doye baat galat ||30||
Datt digambare kab kahyo | je lambo tarkas tir ||
Kalikalman Jivana | bhekh bhayo bepir ||31||
mans gali gali bhuy pade | twacha haad tan jay ||
man gale bin Jivana | Raghupati nahi sahay ||32||
man maskhari chhand de | Sadguru ray sujan ||
bhut pret kaha Jivana | chhodave Jam ran ||33||

|| Iti Shri Bhekhka Ang sampurna ||13||
translation:
Here begins the Chapter of the Religious Garb ||13||

1. The rosary and the tilak mark, Jivan - that is the garb of Vishnu. On the body it makes a fine show, but without Hari the man is a mere corpse.

2. The two are alike, Jivan - the play-actor and the world. He has put on the garb of a devotee, but his appetite has not ceased.

3. Like horns on a sambar's head, such is the garb of the rosary. What sort of fight can there be, Jivan, where there is no mark of warrior blood?

4. Trusting in the rosary, Jivan, the whole lifetime went barren. Of Sitapati Raghunath there was not so much as a sound in a dream.

5. I would cut off the hand of that servant who makes a display of tying on a rosary. Without Ram's Name, Jivan, the garb has made buffoons of them all.

6. He puts on two or four rosaries and the fool rejoices in his heart. She is a widow - for nothing she flaunts her charms.

7. A long rosary of japa (repetition of the Name), Jivan, is paraded before the world. Our business is with half a Name - the one the Sadguru pointed out.

8. The age in which men crossed over by trusting in the tilak and the tulsi was some other age. Now in the Kaljug it is said - listen, Jivan - without My Name there is no place of rest.

9. Do not pull off your shoes, Jivan, before you have reached the water. If Ram's Name is not in the heart, how shall the world let go of you?

10. Without the philosopher's stone there is no transmuting touch - a common stone does nothing to iron. Without Sitapati, Jivan, both the garb and the learning are in vain.

11. All this garb is a conjuror's trick, and he calls himself a servant of God. Brahma and the rest played that game, Jivan, and in the end went away disappointed.

12. Without Trikam (the Lord) as your reckoning and your resource, what sort of yoga and renunciation is it? That woman is the unloved wife, Jivan; it is Sham (the dark Lord) who gives the good fortune of wifehood.

13. The barren woman fondles another's son and laughing, laughing, sings the songs of blessing; but the boy's own mother, Jivan, closes her mouth and smiles.

14. By what karma, Jivan, did that woman become barren? Yashoda has borne a son, and yet no song of blessing is sung at her door.

15. He has put on the garb of a devotee, but he has no faith in the Name. It is like the barren woman's blessing-song, Jivan - love lavished on another's son.

16. He recites sakhis (couplets) and shabads, but Raghupati's Name is not in them. It is a craving for ghevar (a rich sweet), Jivan, with not a cowrie's worth of money in the purse.

17. Everyone stitches together a patchwork, joining two syllables to two. By trading in lumps of jaggery, Jivan, how shall one earn lakhs and crores?

18. Picking up two or four lessons here and there, Jivan, he goes forth and becomes a pandit; such a one never reaches the far shore.

19. Offer the mind at the Guru's feet; the body stays among the five elements and the clan. Brahma and the rest go astray in this, Jivan - that way one is not called a Harijan (a devotee of Hari).

20. This is a hard thing to swallow, Jivan - that caste, sub-caste and lineage should go. It is a matter beyond all other matters; even Brahma and the rest went away cheated of it.

21. When loss and gain come, Jivan, everyone takes to renunciation; and then they became just what they were before - moustache on the face, turban on the head.

22. He wears the Kaustubh jewel at his throat, and among it, here and there, a dog's bones. So it is, Jivan, when in the devotion of Ram one keeps the impressions of other gods (Anadev).

23. The renunciate without discrimination begs alms from door to door. Hari gives everything, Jivan, to the one who takes the Guru's teaching to heart.

24. He licks up the world's leavings and carries pride in his mind. This is not the Guru's grace, Jivan - it is a dog wandering from door to door.

25. The mind has not been shaved, Jivan; then what is gained by shaving the head? He looks like a widow - neither a man nor a woman.

26. What is gained by having the head shaved, or by letting the hair grow long? The "I" does not go, Jivan, without the Sadguru's teaching.

27. He wears the tilak, offers his salutations, takes a red staff in his hand: this is Yama's herdsman, listen Jivan - he drives the whole herd along with him.

28. As the tuft of hair on a tail, so is the moustache. Without Ram's Name, Jivan, such is the moustache on his face.

29. Everyone utters Ram's Name, each by his own reckoning. But the "I" does not go, Jivan - how then shall one escape the four kinds of birth?

30. All the yogis speak of Gorakh, and the sannyasis speak of Datt. Without the religion of the soul, Jivan, both claims are false.

31. When did Datta the naked one ever tell them to carry a long quiver and arrows? In the Kali age, Jivan, the religious garb has grown shameless.

32. The flesh may rot away and fall to the ground; skin, bone and body may all go. But without the mind melting, Jivan, Raghupati does not come to help.

33. O mind, give up your mockery; the Sadguru is a wise king. What are ghosts and spirits, Jivan - he sets you free even from Yama the king.

|| Here the Chapter of the Religious Garb is complete ||13||
